scope: One-paragraph educational field notes. The sentences are habitat-search guidance or source-reported synthesis, not a habitat suitability model, preference study, confirmed new locality, or rarity-tier input.
displayRule: One paragraph per species; insert field cue before trailing DENR status where present.

records.fieldCue: Shaded canopy gaps and streamside trees offer concealed hunting perches for this baza.
records.anchor: The Jerdon's Baza is reported from forests, rivers and streams, as well as grasslands and other open areas.

records.fieldCue: During seasonal movements, wooded ridgelines and openings along forest margins can bring passing Grey-faced Buzzards into view.
records.anchor: The Grey-faced Buzzard is reported from forests.

records.fieldCue: Pied Harriers search low over wet grassland, marsh margins and fallow fields.
records.anchor: The Pied Harrier is reported from freshwater wetlands, grasslands and other open areas, as well as agricultural land.

records.fieldCue: Reedbeds, flooded grassland and marsh edges provide hunting space for Eastern Marsh Harriers quartering over wetland vegetation.
records.anchor: The Eastern Marsh Harrier has been reported from Mindanao, Siargao and Leyte.

records.fieldCue: Open fields with isolated trees and poles provide hunting perches for Black-winged Kites, which also hover while searching for prey.
records.anchor: The Black-winged Kite is reported from grasslands and other open areas, shrublands, agricultural areas, as well as settlements and disturbed habitats.

records.fieldCue: Along estuaries, Brahminy Kites patrol mangrove margins, tidal flats and channels, taking food from the water and exposed shoreline.
records.anchor: The Brahminy Kite occurs along coasts, especially mangroves and estuaries, and is sometimes seen over forests and inland rivers (Australian Museum, 2024).

records.fieldCue: Large, slow-moving rivers and wetlands with tall bankside trees provide perches overlooking the water for Grey-headed Fish Eagles.
records.anchor: The Grey-headed Fish Eagle inhabits freshwater environments, particularly large slow rivers, reservoirs and wetlands (BirdLife International, 2024).

records.fieldCue: Coastal inlets, sheltered bays and broad river mouths combine open hunting water with elevated perches used by White-bellied Sea Eagles.
records.anchor: The White-bellied Sea Eagle occurs around coastal and inland waterways, using elevated tree perches and soaring over water and adjacent land (Australian Museum, 2022).

records.fieldCue: Shaded forest tracks and small canopy openings provide glimpses into the mid-storey where this goshawk hunts from cover.
records.anchor: Hunts from concealed canopy or mid-storey perches, making rapid attacks on birds, lizards and large insects (Bird Society of Singapore, n.d.).

records.fieldCue: Wooded slopes and openings in the upper forest canopy offer views of Rufous-bellied Eagles moving above the trees.
records.anchor: The Rufous-bellied Eagle is reported from forests.

records.fieldCue: Changeable Hawk-Eagles soar above wooded hills and forest margins and hunt from concealed tree perches.
records.anchor: The Changeable Hawk-Eagle hunts from concealed perches in wooded habitats.

records.fieldCue: Lowland and lower-montane forest, including mature wooded slopes and some selectively disturbed stands, form the main setting for Pinsker's Hawk-Eagle.
records.anchor: Pinsker’s Hawk-Eagle inhabits lowland and lower-montane forest, including selectively logged or otherwise disturbed stands.

records.fieldCue: Wooded ridge crests and canopy openings provide broad views of Crested Honey Buzzards during seasonal movements.
records.anchor: The Crested Honey Buzzard locates bee and wasp colonies and raids their nests for larvae.

records.fieldCue: The Philippine Honey Buzzard uses wooded landscapes, including upper-canopy perches and gaps between tree crowns.
records.anchor: The Philippine Honey Buzzard is reported from forests.

records.fieldCue: On Mindanao, Philippine Eagle nesting landscapes include large emergent trees above wooded slopes and ravines in lowland and upper hill forest.
records.anchor: On Mindanao, Philippine Eagles nest in large trees within lowland dipterocarp and upper hill forest, and some nests occur near the transition to montane or mossy forest.

records.fieldCue: Philippine Serpent Eagles use forest edges, wooded foothills and riparian corridors, where their calls carry across canopy openings.
records.anchor: The Philippine Serpent Eagle is reported from forest edges, riparian forest, foothills and wooded agricultural country (Department of Environment and Natural Resources, n.d.).

records.fieldCue: Narrow gaps in wooded hillsides and forest margins offer brief views of Japanese Sparrowhawks during passage.
records.anchor: The Japanese Sparrowhawk is reported from forests, grasslands and other open habitats.

records.fieldCue: During migration, Chinese Sparrowhawks may appear over wooded valleys and forest margins.
records.anchor: The Chinese Sparrowhawk is reported from forests, grasslands and other open habitats.

records.fieldCue: Within shaded forest, the Besra may perch in the mid-canopy before flying through narrow gaps between trees.
records.anchor: The Besra is reported from forests, grasslands and other open habitats.

records.fieldCue: Over reservoirs, river reaches and coastal shallows, Ospreys search open water and dive to seize fish.
records.anchor: The Osprey is reported from rivers and streams as well as coastal and intertidal habitats.

records.fieldCue: Shallow marshes and seasonally flooded grasslands offer open water and vegetated edges used by Northern Pintails.
records.anchor: The Northern Pintail is reported from freshwater wetlands.

records.fieldCue: Philippine Ducks use inland and coastal wetlands, including small ponds, tidal creeks and larger open-water areas.
records.anchor: The Philippine Duck uses inland and coastal wetlands throughout its Philippine range (BirdLife International, 2016).

records.fieldCue: Sheltered wetland backwaters and flooded vegetation may provide feeding and resting areas for Eastern Spot-billed Ducks.
records.anchor: The Eastern Spot-billed Duck is reported from freshwater and coastal wetland habitats.

records.fieldCue: Wandering Whistling Ducks gather on freshwater marshes and lakes, often among patches of emergent vegetation.
records.anchor: The Wandering Whistling Duck has been documented on Mindanao, Samar, Leyte, Bohol, and Siargao.

records.fieldCue: Spotted Whistling Ducks use tree-bordered wetlands and freshwater marshes, with historical Philippine observations also extending to coastal marsh.
records.anchor: The Spotted Whistling Duck is reported from forest and freshwater wetlands, with a historical record from coastal marsh near Zamboanga.

records.fieldCue: Forested mountain streams provide wet rock surfaces and nearby vegetation that may shelter McGregor's Slender Stream Toad.
records.anchor: The McGregor's Slender Stream Toad has been documented on Mindanao, including Mount Kitanglad Range, Mount Malindang Range, Pasonanca area, Zamboanga del Norte, and Zamboanga del Sur (GBIF.org, 2026; Beukema, 2011; AMNH Amphibian Species of the World, n.d.; AMNH, n.d.; Nuñeza et al., 2010).

records.fieldCue: Shaded stream corridors with boulders and shallow riffles may provide refuge and activity sites for Müller's Slender Stream Toad.
records.anchor: Hilong-hilong surveys documented specimens on forest-floor leaf litter, in rocky crevices and along stream banks between about 700 and 1,300 m (Sanguila et al., 2016).

records.fieldCue: Western Mindanao Toadlets have been observed on sapling and shrub leaves near streams, including moderately disturbed forest edges.
records.anchor: The Western Mindanao Toadlet has been observed on leaves of saplings and shrubs near streams, including forest edges and other moderately disturbed areas.

records.fieldCue: Low ferns and shrub leaves form recorded perches for the Eastern Mindanao Toadlet in montane forest.
records.anchor: The Eastern Mindanao Toadlet has been observed on low ferns and shrub leaves in montane forest in the Leyte Cordillera (Decena et al., 2023).

records.fieldCue: Marine Toads often occupy disturbed lowland areas, including yards, drainage edges and temporary pools that fill after rain.
records.anchor: In Agusan Marsh it was recorded around agricultural margins and mixed freshwater-swamp vegetation (Sanguila et al., 2026).

records.fieldCue: Within limestone forest, shaded leaf litter and sheltered rock crevices may provide moist refuges for Walter's Limestone Forest Frog.
records.anchor: Walter’s Limestone Forest Frog inhabits the forest floor and terrestrial limestone habitats of eastern Samar (Siler et al., 2009).

records.fieldCue: The forest floor is a documented habitat of the Masked Wrinkled Ground Frog, including terrestrial sites away from immediate stream margins.
records.anchor: In the Taguibo Watershed survey, specimens identified as Platymantis corrugatus were recorded on ground-level habitats in the terrestrial zone away from immediate stream margins.

records.fieldCue: Broad leaves and low branches in humid forest may offer sheltered perches for Günther's Wrinkled Tree Frog.
records.anchor: In Agusan peat-swamp forest, calling frogs perched 1–3 m above the ground, while a northeastern Leyte survey recorded calling males on ferns, small branches and other low vegetation (Sanguila et al., 2026; Decena et al., 2023).

records.fieldCue: The Mindanao Variable Forest Frog has been recorded on the floor of mature forest at Mount Hilong-Hilong.
records.anchor: The Mindanao Variable Forest Frog has been recorded on the forest floor of mature forest on Mount Hilong-hilong (Frost, 2026).

records.fieldCue: Shaded ground cover and deep leaf litter in terrestrial forest may shelter Jagor's Variable Forest Frog.
records.anchor: Jagor’s Variable Forest Frog is associated with terrestrial forest habitats in the southern Philippines.

records.fieldCue: In northeastern Mindanao, fallen wood and leaf litter may create sheltered spaces for this broad-headed forest frog.
records.anchor: The Broad-headed Variable Forest Frog inhabits terrestrial forest habitats in northeastern Mindanao.

records.fieldCue: Cloudy montane forest provides a cool, damp setting for Navjot Sodhi's Cloud Frog, with shaded vegetation offering possible activity sites after rain.
records.anchor: Navjot Sodhi’s Cloud Frog inhabits montane forest on Leyte and has also been recorded from northern Leyte and north-central Samar (Diesmos et al., 2020; Frost, 2026).

records.fieldCue: Rabor's Horned Tree Frog calls high in the forest canopy and has also been recorded on vegetation in Mindanao surveys.
records.anchor: Rabor’s Horned Tree Frog often calls high in the forest canopy, producing slowly repeated pulsed notes; Taguibo Watershed surveys also document it on vegetation (Sanguila et al., 2016; Sanguila et al., 2021).

records.fieldCue: Asian Mangrove Frogs may occupy shallow pools and muddy backwaters along mangrove margins, including brackish edges.
records.anchor: The Asian Mangrove Frog has been recorded in ground-level and aquatic habitats on northeastern Leyte (Decena et al., 2023).

records.fieldCue: Rice paddies, irrigation channels, still pools beside streams and swampy forest patches are documented habitats of the Philippine Field Frog.
records.anchor: In the Taguibo Watershed analysis, sampled animals occupied aquatic habitats; northeastern Leyte inventories recorded both terrestrial and aquatic observations.

records.fieldCue: Large pools, wetland margins and flooded cultivated ground provide potential shallow-water habitat for the East Asian Bullfrog.
records.anchor: The East Asian Bullfrog is reported from cultivated areas.

records.fieldCue: White-spined Fanged Frogs have been recorded beside rocky mountain streams, including riparian sites above 900 m.
records.anchor: The species has been reported from higher-elevation riparian forest in Mindanao, including mountain streams above 900 m (Frost, 2026).

records.fieldCue: Fallen logs, rocks, stream margins and the adjoining forest floor provide shelter and activity sites for the Philippine Swamp Frog.
records.anchor: At Tinuy-an Falls, this species was found on fallen logs, the forest floor, and stream margins.

records.fieldCue: Mindanao Fanged Frogs occupy small, shallow forest streams and nearby banks, ground surfaces and low vegetation.
records.anchor: A 2025 anuran survey along Miral River in Bansalan, Davao del Sur, reports the species in a six-species field assemblage (Ubat, 2025).

records.fieldCue: Shaded stream margins and damp ground in riparian forest may provide activity sites for the Western Mindanao Fanged Frog.
records.anchor: Compiled ecological information describes the Western Mindanao Fanged Frog as using terrestrial and aquatic environments and having a larval stage (Oliveira et al., 2017).

records.fieldCue: Streams through lowland and lower-montane forest are reported habitats of the Philippine Guardian Frog.
records.anchor: Reported around streams in undisturbed lowland and lower montane forests of Mindanao (Frost, 2026).

records.fieldCue: The Visayan Fanged Frog may use saturated ground and shallow edges of forest streams within its island range.
records.anchor: Compiled traits describe the Visayan Fanged Frog as nocturnal and associated with both terrestrial and aquatic environments, with larval development (Oliveira et al., 2017).

records.fieldCue: Small puddles and shallow standing water may provide activity sites for this tiny aquatic frog during wet periods.
records.anchor: Compiled ecological information places the Tiny Puddle Frog in terrestrial and aquatic environments, with a larval stage (Oliveira et al., 2017).

records.fieldCue: Common Puddle Frogs occupy shallow water and muddy margins, including small pools and waterlogged ground along lowland tracks.
records.anchor: The Common Puddle Frog has been recorded in aquatic habitats on northeastern Leyte (Decena et al., 2023).

records.fieldCue: In villages and gardens, damp leaf litter, planted beds and sheltered ground cover can support the small terrestrial Greenhouse Frog.
records.anchor: Direct development occurs within terrestrial eggs, with small froglets hatching without an aquatic tadpole stage (Animal Diversity Web, n.d.).

records.fieldCue: Philippine Crocodiles inhabit freshwater marsh channels, vegetated pond margins and calmer river reaches, where basking and shelter sites occur near water.
records.anchor: The Philippine Crocodile inhabits freshwater rivers, creeks, ponds, lakes and marshes.

records.fieldCue: Saltwater Crocodiles move through tidal channels, estuarine banks and mangrove creeks and can travel far into freshwater river reaches.
records.anchor: Saltwater Crocodiles use tidal rivers, estuaries, mangrove swamps and coastal waters, and may also occupy freshwater rivers and lakes well inland.

records.fieldCue: Sunlit branches, forest-edge saplings and adjoining shrub vegetation may offer perches for the Philippine Bloodsucker.
records.anchor: The Philippine Bloodsucker is reported from forests and shrublands.

records.fieldCue: In northeastern Mindanao, Two-spotted Flying Lizards have been recorded on trunks near forest edges and adjoining coconut groves (Sanguila et al., 2016).

newReference.full: Sanguila, M. B., Cobb, K. A., Siler, C. D., Diesmos, A. C., Alcala, A. C., & Brown, R. M. (2016). The amphibians and reptiles of Mindanao Island, southern Philippines, II: The herpetofauna of northeast Mindanao and adjacent islands. ZooKeys, 624, 1–132. https://doi.org/10.3897/zookeys.624.9814

records.anchor: Agusan Marsh records include peat-swamp forest and relatively low perches in regenerating vegetation (Sanguila et al., 2026).

records.fieldCue: Northeastern Mindanao records place Chartreuse-spotted Flying Lizards on coconut palms and exposed trunks adjoining forest (Sanguila et al., 2016).

newReference.full: Sanguila, M. B., Cobb, K. A., Siler, C. D., Diesmos, A. C., Alcala, A. C., & Brown, R. M. (2016). The amphibians and reptiles of Mindanao Island, southern Philippines, II: The herpetofauna of northeast Mindanao and adjacent islands. ZooKeys, 624, 1–132. https://doi.org/10.3897/zookeys.624.9814

records.anchor: Recent survey records from Taguibo Watershed placed Draco cyanopterus in vegetation and trees of the sampled terrestrial zone (Sanguila et al., 2021).

records.fieldCue: Near Malagos, Mindanao, Günther's Flying Lizards used trees in secondary forest and coconut palms beside the forest (McGuire & Alcala, 2000).
records.anchor: Fieldworkers recorded Günther's Flying Lizard in secondary-growth forest and on coconut trees beside the forest near Malagos, Mindanao (McGuire & Alcala, 2000).

records.fieldCue: Daytime observations place Mindanao Flying Lizards on trunks several metres above ground in primary and mature secondary rainforest (Sanguila et al., 2016).
records.anchor: Mindanao Flying Lizards have been observed on tree trunks in primary and mature secondary rainforest; field accounts describe daytime activity several metres above the ground, commonly around 5–10 m (Sanguila et al., 2016).

records.fieldCue: Ornate Flying Lizards have been recorded on trunks in primary and secondary forest and coconut stands close to wooded areas (Sanguila et al., 2016).
records.anchor: Surveys have recorded this flying lizard on trees in primary and secondary forest and in coconut plantings close to forest; northeastern Leyte records include individuals using lowland coconut-plantation vegetation (Sanguila et al., 2016; Decena et al., 2023).

records.fieldCue: Brightly lit coconut palms and exposed tree trunks are documented perches for Reticulated Flying Lizards in plantation landscapes.
records.anchor: In the revision’s field observations, Draco reticulatus occurred mainly in open coconut plantations and was observed using well-sunlit trees on Bohol in sympatry with D. bimaculatus and D. ornatus.

records.fieldCue: At Agusan Marsh, Anglehead Lizards have been recorded in peat-swamp forest, where shaded trunks and nearby vegetation provide potential perches.
records.anchor: In Agusan Marsh, lizards identified as Gonocephalus semperi were encountered in Katigbok peat-swamp forest.

records.fieldCue: Streams and rivers offer escape water and raised bankside perches for Philippine Sailfin Lizards, including branches and exposed trunks.
records.anchor: Recorded on overhanging trees beside streams and riverbanks near Agusan Marsh agricultural land (Sanguila et al., 2026).

records.fieldCue: Asian Vine Snakes use slender branches, vines and shrubs along wooded edges, where their narrow green bodies blend with foliage.
records.anchor: Sleeping snakes were seen on low shrubs beside forest edges (Sanguila et al., 2016).

records.fieldCue: Intertwined branches and lower-canopy vegetation may provide nighttime activity sites for the Philippine Blunt-headed Cat Snake.
records.anchor: The species has been characterized as fully arboreal in comparative snake-habitat literature summarized by Uetz et al (2026).

records.fieldCue: Tree limbs and dense climbing vegetation may offer nighttime hunting routes for the Dog-toothed Cat Snake.
records.anchor: In the Leyte Cordillera and Babatngon ranges, the species was encountered in ground-level habitats (Decena et al., 2023).

records.fieldCue: Mangrove branches and creekside trees above tidal water offer sheltered climbing habitat for the Mangrove Snake.
records.anchor: An adult was documented swimming through a shallow stream at Tinuy-an Falls (Plaza et al., 2025).

records.fieldCue: In shaded forest, slender branches and hanging vegetation may provide nighttime perches for the White-spotted Cat Snake.
records.anchor: The White-spotted Cat Snake is reported from forests.

records.fieldCue: Philippine Reed Snakes have been recorded in soil and beneath forest-floor debris, moving through sheltered ground.
records.anchor: This species was recorded in soil and beneath forest-floor debris (Sanguila et al., 2016).

records.fieldCue: In northeastern Leyte, Variable Reed Snakes have been recorded among riparian boulders and leaf litter in dipterocarp forest.
records.anchor: In northeastern Leyte, the species was recorded in ground-level habitats (Decena et al., 2023).

records.fieldCue: Paradise Flying Snakes move between tree crowns by day, using trunks and connected canopy branches.
records.anchor: This snake is fully arboreal and uses the tree canopy and branches (Uetz et al., 2026).

records.fieldCue: Fallen wood, ground cover and vegetated forest edges may provide retreat and movement sites for the Philippine Red-tailed Ratsnake.
records.anchor: In the Leyte Cordillera and Babatngon ranges, the species was encountered in aquatic habitats (Decena et al., 2023).

records.fieldCue: The sunlit shrub layer and lower trees around forest openings may provide activity sites for Maren's Bronzeback Snake.
records.anchor: Tree-dwelling specimens were recorded from the Agusan region (Sanguila et al., 2016).

records.fieldCue: Philippine Bronzeback Snakes may move through shrubs and connected branches around forest gaps.
records.anchor: The Philippine Bronzeback Snake is reported from forests.

records.fieldCue: Fine branches, suspended vines and dense shrubs offer likely climbing routes for the Philippine Whip Snake.
records.anchor: The Philippine Whip Snake is reported from forests.

records.fieldCue: Trees and climbing plants at wooded edges create connected aboveground pathways for the Red-tailed Green Ratsnake.
records.anchor: The Red-tailed Green Ratsnake is recorded on Mindanao, Samar, Leyte, Bohol, and Dinagat.

records.fieldCue: Common Wolf Snakes use sheltered ground, rock crevices and modified lowland surroundings, including areas near houses.
records.anchor: The Common Wolf Snake has been recorded near residences and other heavily modified lowland sites (Sanguila et al., 2016).

records.fieldCue: Philippine Brown Deer browse shoots and foliage in forest clearings and adjoining grassland, often moving along sheltered vegetated paths.
records.anchor: The Philippine Brown Deer browses shoots, foliage and fruit and may graze in forest clearings and adjacent grassland.

records.fieldCue: On the forest floor, rooted soil, wallows and disturbed leaf litter may reveal movements of Philippine Warty Pigs.
records.anchor: The Philippine Warty Pig inhabits forests and adjoining vegetated habitats, including montane and mossy forest in some areas.

records.fieldCue: Fruiting trees and connecting branches in woodland provide likely nighttime feeding and movement routes for the Philippine Palm Civet.
records.anchor: The Philippine Palm Civet is reported from forests.

records.fieldCue: Malay Civets travel along ground-level routes through secondary woodland, cultivated edges and other vegetated mosaics.
records.anchor: The Malay Civet uses forest, cultivated land and other modified terrestrial habitats.

records.fieldCue: Small Asian Sheath-tailed Bats roost in caves and partly lit rock cavities, including recorded sites on Siargao and in the Agusan region.
records.anchor: The Small Asian Sheath-tailed Bat roosts in caves, including partly lit cavities, on Siargao and in the Agusan provinces of Mindanao.

records.fieldCue: Bare-rumped Sheath-tailed Bats shelter in hollow trees, rock cracks and buildings and emerge after dusk to forage over nearby landscapes.
records.anchor: The Bare-rumped Sheath-tailed Bat roosts in hollow trees, rock crevices and buildings.

records.fieldCue: Black-bearded Tomb Bats shelter in cave recesses and narrow rock crevices, sometimes gathering in maternity groups.
records.anchor: The Black-bearded Tomb Bat roosts in cave crevices and cavities, sometimes forming maternity groups.

records.fieldCue: Caves and karst may provide daytime shelter for Philippine Tailless Roundleaf Bats, with adjoining forest and waterways offering possible flight corridors.
records.anchor: The Philippine Tailless Roundleaf Bat is reported from forests, rivers, streams, caves and karst landscapes.

records.fieldCue: In forested karst country, cave chambers may provide daytime roosts for Philippine Dusky Roundleaf Bats.
records.anchor: The Philippine Dusky Roundleaf Bat is reported from forests, caves, and karst areas.

records.fieldCue: Fawn-colored Roundleaf Bats have been recorded in caves on Siargao and in Agusan del Sur, where sheltered chambers provide roosting space.
records.anchor: The Fawn-colored Roundleaf Bat has been recorded roosting in caves on Siargao and in Agusan del Sur (Nuñeza & Galorio, 2014; Perez & Nuñeza, 2020).

records.fieldCue: Large Mindanao Roundleaf Bats are reported from forested karst landscapes, where sheltered cave spaces may be used for roosting.
records.anchor: The Large Mindanao Roundleaf Bat is reported from forests, caves and karst landscapes.

records.fieldCue: Diadem Roundleaf Bats have documented cave roosts on Mindanao and Siargao amid wooded landscapes.
records.anchor: The Diadem Roundleaf Bat roosts in caves on Siargao and Mindanao.

records.fieldCue: Philippine Forest Roundleaf Bats occur from lowland to montane forest on Mindanao, with records reaching about 1,100 m elevation.
records.anchor: On Mindanao, the Philippine Forest Roundleaf Bat occurs in primary and disturbed lowland forest and has been documented in montane forest to about 1,100 m.

records.fieldCue: Large hollow trees, including dao, provide recorded shelters for Lesser Asian False-vampires, which also roost in caves and buildings.
records.anchor: The Lesser Asian False-vampire roosts in caves, hollow trees and sometimes buildings.

records.fieldCue: Little Long-fingered Bats shelter by day in caves, tunnels and abandoned mines before moving through nearby airspace after dusk.
records.anchor: The Little Long-fingered Bat uses caves, abandoned mines, tunnels and other cavities as day roosts.

records.fieldCue: Caves within forested karst may provide roosting spaces for Great Long-fingered Bats, with wooded corridors forming possible flight routes.
records.anchor: The Great Long-fingered Bat is reported from forests, caves and karst landscapes.

records.fieldCue: Philippine records include Lesser Naked Bats roosting in hollow trees and coconut palms, with occasional cave use.
records.anchor: In the Philippines, the Lesser Naked Bat has been found roosting in hollow trees and coconut palms, as well as occasionally in caves (IUCN, 2019).

records.fieldCue: Wrinkle-lipped Free-tailed Bats form colonies in caves and can also occupy rock crevices and buildings.
records.anchor: The Wrinkle-lipped Free-tailed Bat roosts in caves, sometimes in large colonies, and also uses rock crevices and buildings.

records.fieldCue: Openings above wooded waterways and cultivated land may provide flight corridors for Sulawesian Free-tailed Bats.
records.anchor: The Sulawesian Free-tailed Bat is reported from forests, rivers and streams, and cultivated areas.

records.fieldCue: A Luzon GPS study found most recorded foraging locations of Golden-capped Flying Foxes in closed forest, with roosting trees occurring across a wider landscape (de Jong et al., 2013).

newReference.full: de Jong, C., Field, H., Tagtag, A., Hughes, T., Dechmann, D., Jayme, S., et al. (2013). Foraging behaviour and landscape utilisation by the endangered golden-crowned flying fox (Acerodon jubatus), the Philippines. PLOS ONE, 8(11), e79665. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0079665

records.anchor: The Golden-capped Flying Fox roosts in trees, sometimes alongside other large flying foxes, and feeds heavily on figs in mature lowland forest.

records.fieldCue: High-elevation mossy forest on Mount Kitanglad is a documented habitat of the Mindanao Pygmy Fruit Bat.
records.anchor: The Mindanao Pygmy Fruit Bat occurs in montane forest, with Mount Kitanglad records particularly numerous in high-elevation mossy forest.

records.fieldCue: Fruiting and flowering vegetation provides food for Lesser Short-nosed Fruit Bats, while leaves, trees and buildings offer daytime roosts.
records.anchor: The Lesser Short-nosed Fruit Bat feeds on fruit and nectar and may roost under leaves, in trees or in buildings.

records.fieldCue: Fruiting trees in the forest canopy may provide feeding opportunities for the White-winged Flying Fox.
records.anchor: The White-winged Flying Fox is reported from forests.

records.fieldCue: Philippine Large-headed Fruit Bats may forage among fruiting trees and connected upper-canopy vegetation in forest.
records.anchor: The Philippine Large-headed Fruit Bat is reported from forests.

records.fieldCue: Flowering forest plants provide nectar-feeding opportunities for the Philippine Dawn Bat during nighttime activity.
records.anchor: The Philippine Dawn Bat feeds on nectar and can pollinate forest trees, linking its foraging ecology to flowering plants (Roño et al., 2021).

styleNote: Habitat detail written as flowing, declarative natural-history prose. Inferences remain qualified without repetitive disclaimers.
placement: Anchor is an exact natural-history sentence in the v1.76 account after v1.78 readability refinements. insert and replace are used only if unique; retain avoids duplicate coverage already in the published paragraph.
